title: 1 Corinthians: a gifted church, coming apart
note: Rebuilt on 2026-11-26 from the Bible Explorer film of the same slug. New wording, same facts: each claim is in the old film's captions or its 'differ' note, whose sources are in docs/work/elite/explorer-ledger.md. Scripture is the Berean Standard Bible, checked against client/public/bible/text/ by film/tools/write-script.py.

lines: First Corinthians is a real letter to a real church with real trouble. The church in Corinth was young, rich in gifts and eloquent speech, and coming apart.
Paul neither gives up on it nor flatters it.

scripture.text: To the church of God in Corinth, to those sanctified in Christ Jesus and called to be holy

lines: Chapters one to six answer what Paul has heard by report. Chapters seven to sixteen answer the questions the Corinthians wrote to him, many marked by the words now about.
The letter begins with the cross and ends with the resurrection.

scripture.text: Now for the matters you wrote about

lines: Corinth prized eloquence, knowledge, and status. Paul answers with a crucified Messiah, which looked like foolishness.
For I resolved to know nothing while I was with you except Jesus Christ and Him crucified.
The cross doesn't only save. It reorders what counts as strength and wisdom.

scripture.text: For I resolved to know nothing while I was with you except Jesus Christ and Him crucified.

lines: The Spirit gives varied gifts to one body for the common good. Division is not a matter of taste. It's an attack on what God is building.
Now you are the body of Christ, and each of you is a member of it.
Unity is not sameness, and the weaker members are indispensable.

scripture.text: Now you are the body of Christ, and each of you is a member of it.

lines: Chapter thirteen is often read at weddings. In its setting it's a rebuke to a church competing over spiritual gifts.
Love is patient, love is kind.
Knowledge puffs up. Love builds up. Without love, even the most impressive gifts amount to nothing.

scripture.text: Love is patient, love is kind.

lines: Some in Corinth denied that the dead rise. Paul restates the gospel. Christ died, was buried, was raised on the third day, and appeared to many.
But Christ has indeed been raised from the dead.
His rising is the firstfruits of all who belong to him.

scripture.text: But Christ has indeed been raised from the dead

lines: Some passages are hard, and faithful churches reach different answers: marriage, singleness, and divorce in chapter seven, head coverings in worship in chapter eleven, and gifts like tongues and the place of women in leading worship in chapters twelve to fourteen.
Readers weigh whether Paul grounds his words in creation, the gospel, or the custom of the day, and they weigh them differently. This film takes no side.
Start with chapters one to four, read as one piece.
Ask of each chapter: what has the crucified and risen Lord to do with this?
Paul's counsel near the end is short.
Do everything in love.
